about: Column widths set on columns, and how insertion and deletion carry them (ADR-0046, ADR-0047, SH-22). A width is in Excel's unit, characters of the default font; setColumnWidth sets the columns its range spans, as Range.ColumnWidth does, and a null width puts them back at the standard width (Range.UseStandardWidth). width is the check column's recorded width, null where none is recorded, which Excel reports as its standard width (8.43). Microsoft documents Range.ColumnWidth in characters, setting it on every column of a range, 8.43 as the default and 255 as the widest; Excel snaps a width to whole pixels, so the cases use whole numbers. Microsoft documents that an inserted column takes the formatting of the column to its left (Insert Options, Format Same As Left), but not whether its width is part of that, nor how deletion moves widths: those cases are uncertain until the oracle asks Excel. custom says whether the check column's width is marked custom, Excel's customWidth attribute of a column in its files, which ECMA-376 documents as false when absent; the oracle reads it from a saved copy. A recorded width is one of two kinds, both marked custom (ADR-0046, 2026-09-28): one the user set (a drag, a size to fit, sizeToFit, which the oracle does as AutoFit, or a command), which an entry never widens, and one a typed entry widened the column to (CW-018, CW-027..029), which a longer entry widens again (CW-028). A width widened by entry (automatic) is set by nothing in Excel but a typed entry, so the oracle blocks those cases. A case with widens, widthAtMost or widthAtLeast is typed: the oracle types it with real keys (ask by keys), its own cells and its enter actions, and the engine harness widens the typed cell's column after each of them as the component does, recording the width as widened by entry in the engine's characters. widthAtMost and widthAtLeast bound the check column's width when the case is read, in characters; widthAtLeast asks whether a longer entry widens a column again. Excel's width for a typed entry is its own pixels' (12345678901 widened a column to 11.18 at 150% in the seventeenth Windows run, b10), so a typed case bounds the width rather than naming it. A column inserted beside a width widened by entry takes it as a width the user set: Excel writes the inserted column customWidth without bestFit, the flag ECMA-376 gives a column a typed number widens again, while the column to its left keeps bestFit (b10, CW-023). Deletion and undo keep a width's kind (CW-025, CW-026).

cases.description: A column nobody set is at the standard width, and records none
A width set on a column is that column's width
A width set on a range of cells is set on every column the range spans
Setting one column's width leaves its neighbour at the standard width
A column put back at the standard width records none
An inserted column takes the width of the column to its left, as it takes its formats
A column's width moves right with it when columns are inserted before it
A column inserted after a column at the standard width is at the standard width, whatever the column it pushed right
A column inserted at A has no column to its left, and is at the standard width
Deleting a column moves the widths to its right left with their columns
Deleting columns drops their widths: the column that moves into their place brings its own
Inserting rows leaves the column widths alone
Undoing a width puts back the standard width (asked by hand: verification/2026-10-11-windows-17, b9)
Undoing a column's deletion puts back its width (asked by hand: verification/2026-10-11-windows-17, b9)
The widest column Excel allows is 255 characters
A width the user sets is custom
A column nobody set records no width, and is not custom

A typed number that widens its column makes the width custom, as Excel's file marks it (verification/2026-09-27-windows-excel-2: widened to 10.18, customWidth set; ADR-0047, "What the second observation settled"). The engine leaves the widening to the component; the harness widens as the component does

cases.description: Size to fit is a width the user set: custom, like a drag (the engine is handed the width the component fitted; Excel fits its own, so only the flag is compared)

A typed number that widens its column is recorded as a width widened by entry, marked custom as Excel's file marks it (ADR-0046, 2026-09-28): typed, Excel widened B to 11.18, written width="11.81640625" bestFit="1" customWidth="1" (verification/2026-10-11-windows-17, b10). Excel's width for a typed entry is in its own pixels (11.18 at 150%), and the engine harness's is its characters (11), so the width is bounded, not compared
